newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close weaker in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close weaker in active trade.

text.p: MILAN, Jan 27 - Italian shares closed mostly weaker on Monday, dragged down by bellwether stocks ENI and Fiat, which beat a retreat on profit-taking, while Olivetti took a fresh pummelling on fears a key division had swung into loss.
The blue chip Mib30 was 0.46 percent down at 18,479 while the all-share Mibtel lost 0.31 percent to finish at 12,379.

ENI shed 1.26 percent to 8,840 lire, Fiat eased 1.02 percent to 5,320 lire while Olivetti dropped 8.43 percent to 658 lire. Olivetti had risen last week after the announcement of the sale of its troubled PCs business.
Brokers said Olivetti's decline was driven by rumours that the group's systems and services division, one of the mainstays of the business, had made a net loss in 1996.

Stet finished 2.61 percent lower at 7,677 lire following Friday's announcement that it would absorb Telecom Italia as investors switched into savings stock which closed 3.55 percent higher at 6,093 lire.
Bulgari dropped 4.66 percent to 29,986 lire in a sell-off after the company reported turnover rising 17 percent in 1996 to 449 billion lire, in line with market expectations.
Snia closed 5.69 percent down at 1,775 lire after last Friday's announcement that it was merging with Snia Fibre.
